english: Let $D$, $E$ and $F$ be the midpoints of the sides $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$, respectively, of a triangle $ABC$. Three of the six points $A,B,C,D,E,F$ are chosen at random. Then the probability that the three chosen points are the vertices of a triangle whose area is one-fourth of the area of triangle $ABC$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $D$, $E$ तथा $F$ क्रमशः त्रिभुज $ABC$ की भुजाओं $BC$, $CA$ तथा $AB$ के मध्य-बिन्दु हैं। छः बिन्दुओं $A,B,C,D,E,F$ में से तीन बिन्दु यादृच्छया चुने जाते हैं। तब चुने गए तीनों बिन्दुओं के एक ऐसे त्रिभुज के शीर्ष होने की प्रायिकता, जिसका क्षेत्रफल त्रिभुज $ABC$ के क्षेत्रफल का एक-चौथाई है, ______ है।
solution: 3 vertices: area $\Delta$ (1). 2 vertices + 1 midpoint: on their side collinear (3), else $\dfrac{\Delta}{2}$ (6)
1 vertex + 2 midpoints (9): e.g. $AEF$, $ADE$, $ADF$ all have area $\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$; 3 midpoints: $DEF$, area $\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$ (1)
solution_full: There are $\binom{6}{3}=20$ choices. Let $\Delta$ be the area of triangle $ABC$. Classify by the number of vertices of $ABC$ chosen.

Two vertices and one midpoint ($3\cdot3=9$ choices): if the midpoint is on the side joining the two vertices (e.g. $A,B,F$), the points are collinear (3 choices); otherwise (e.g. $A,B,D$) the triangle has half the base or half the height of a triangle of area $\Delta$, e.g. $[ABD]=\dfrac{1}{2}[ABC]$, area $\dfrac{\Delta}{2}$ (6 choices).

One vertex and two midpoints ($3\cdot3=9$ choices), say vertex $A$: $[AEF]=\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$ (corner triangle); $[ADE]=\dfrac{1}{2}[ADC]=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\Delta}{2}=\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$ since $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$; similarly $[ADF]=\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$. By symmetry all 9 have area $\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$.
Three midpoints: the medial triangle $DEF$, area $\dfrac{\Delta}{4}$ (1 choice).
originality_note: New: the triangles formed by the vertices and side-midpoints of a triangle, classified by area, where the less obvious triangles ADE (vertex with the far midpoint) also have area one-fourth (way 4: a hidden equality of areas). Closest known: 'number of triangles from the vertices and midpoints of a triangle (17)'. Different because: the count is by area, not by non-collinearity, and the vertex-plus-far-midpoint cases must be computed.
blueprint_concepts: Number of straight lines and triangles formed by points

concept_use.Number of straight lines and triangles f: The 20 triples of the six points are classified by how many vertices they contain; the 3 collinear triples are excluded and the areas of the other triangles compared.

key_step: Classifying the triples by the number of original vertices and computing the area ratios.
